Treat the next food as containing egg too and change the records.
Clean using the specified method to prevent allergen carryover.
Use the utensils as they are if the surface color has not changed.
food-1-q004.explanation: Clean utensils used for ingredients containing allergens to prevent the allergens from getting into the next food.
optionExplanations: Skipping the specified cleaning does not prevent carryover.
You cannot resolve the issue by treating the product as something different from what it actually is.
Clean utensils used for ingredients containing allergens to prevent the allergens from getting into the next food.
Appearance alone does not tell you whether allergens remain.

food-1-q005.prompt: Why is keeping received fish at an appropriate low temperature important for controlling histamine?
options: Low temperatures eliminate the need for ingredient history records.
Histamine is a metal fragment.
It eliminates the need to read the fish label.
Poor storage conditions may allow histamine levels to increase.
food-1-q005.explanation: Refrigerate or freeze fish promptly after receiving it to prevent histamine from increasing as storage conditions deteriorate.
optionExplanations: Temperature control and history records are separate controls.

Even with low-temperature control, you still need to check labels and receiving conditions.
Refrigerate or freeze fish promptly after receiving it to prevent histamine from increasing as storage conditions deteriorate.

food-1-q006.prompt: What is the main reason for removing potato sprouts and green skin during preparation?

To prevent food poisoning from solanine.
Only to reduce freezer electricity costs.
To make packaging adhesive stronger.
food-1-q006.explanation: Potato sprouts and green skin contain solanine, so remove those parts.
optionExplanations: This is not an adjustment to metal detection sensitivity.
Potato sprouts and green skin contain solanine, so remove those parts.
The main purpose is to prevent food poisoning from harmful substances.
Removing sprouts and skin is unrelated to packaging adhesion.

food-1-q007.prompt: Which food poisoning prevention principle is keeping food at a low temperature to suppress the growth of food poisoning bacteria?
options: Kill them.
Do not let them multiply.
Delete the records.
Keep them off the food.

optionExplanations: Cold storage mainly suppresses growth and is different from killing bacteria.
Low-temperature control prevents bacteria from multiplying. Do not confuse chilling with killing bacteria.
Deleting records is not a prevention principle.

food-1-q008.prompt: Is it correct to assume that heating always removes toxins produced by bacteria?
options: Yes. All toxins disappear under the same conditions.
Yes. Ingredients with an unusual smell can be used after heating alone.
No. Some toxins are not destroyed by heating.
Yes. Storage control before heating is no longer needed.
food-1-q008.explanation: Some toxins produced by bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus are heat-resistant, so controlling bacterial growth is important.
optionExplanations: Some toxins are heat-resistant, so this absolute claim is incorrect.
Heating alone does not establish that abnormal ingredients are safe.
Some toxins produced by bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus are heat-resistant, so controlling bacterial growth is important.
Storage control is needed to prevent toxin production.

food-1-q009.prompt: Which statement about norovirus matches the training material?
options: It does not multiply in food; it multiplies in the intestines of infected people.
It is a large insect visible to the naked eye.
Only storage temperature needs to be controlled, rather than handwashing.
It multiplies rapidly in all frozen foods.
food-1-q009.explanation: Norovirus control requires keeping it out, keeping it off food, destroying it, and preventing its spread.
optionExplanations: Norovirus control requires keeping it out, keeping it off food, destroying it, and preventing its spread.

The statement that it multiplies in food is incorrect.

food-1-q010.prompt: Mold has grown on an ingredient in storage. What is the appropriate decision?
options: Send it to production without telling the next operator.
Do not use it.
Use it as it is if the color is pale.
Mix in the visible parts to hide them.
food-1-q010.explanation: The training material states that moldy food must not be used.
optionExplanations: Do not use moldy food; follow workplace procedures.
The training material states that moldy food must not be used.
Color intensity alone does not determine whether it can be used.

food-1-q011.prompt: Tool locations and quantities are labeled so that the tools needed can be retrieved immediately. Which activity is this mainly?

Heat treatment to kill microorganisms.
Set in order.
Clean.
food-1-q011.explanation: Setting in order means deciding locations, order, names, quantities, and similar details so items are ready when needed.
optionExplanations: Sorting mainly means removing unnecessary items and keeping only what is needed.
Labeling storage locations does not kill microorganisms through heating.
Setting in order means deciding locations, order, names, quantities, and similar details so items are ready when needed.
Cleaning is the activity of removing dirt.

food-1-q012.prompt: Someone is about to bring a container of untreated ingredients into an area where food is handled after heating. What is the main concern?
options: Work records will no longer be necessary.
There is a risk of cross-contamination.
All food will automatically be frozen.
The product will always lose weight.
food-1-q012.explanation: Follow area boundaries and movement routes to prevent dirt from ingredients or containers from reaching clean food.
optionExplanations: Crossing an area boundary does not eliminate the need for records.
Follow area boundaries and movement routes to prevent dirt from ingredients or containers from reaching clean food.

food-1-q013.prompt: A chemical container has no name label. What should you do?
options: Do not use it; report it to the person in charge.
Move it to the ingredient storeroom and place it beside food.
Identify it by smelling it.
Mix it with another chemical and use it.
food-1-q013.explanation: Chemicals must be labeled so their names can be identified. Report any unlabeled chemical to the person in charge immediately.
optionExplanations: Chemicals must be labeled so their names can be identified. Report any unlabeled chemical to the person in charge immediately.

food-1-q014.prompt: You develop stomach pain and diarrhea while working. What should you do?
